commentary_segments.text: In many applications, operational amplifiers are required which have three stages. For example, class AB amplifiers have an output stage which provide little gain but a lot of current. The first two stages are now needed to provide gain. Also, when the supply voltage is less than 1 V, more stages are required as cascoding is no longer possible. In this Chapter, the principles are discussed to stabilize three-stage amplifiers. Moreover, circuit principles are devised to reduce the power consumption.
